Raising the CLI file-level worker count by itself: the runner already executes the slow file concurrently with the rest of the CLI project.

Treating the lane total or the slow file total as evidence of which internal phase dominates; the current timers measure broader invocations.
Moving any of the twelve files to parallel based only on filenames or source structure; the current evidence does not demonstrate independence under load.

Treating the sequential shard runner as a proven import-time optimization; its source documents a different purpose and separate process starts.
Counting source-level reads alone cannot show the elapsed-time saving; the scan cost must be measured on the target workload.

Enabling the cache at the CLI gateway solely because repeated ledger reads are visible in source; there is no test-cycle profile showing their cost and the gateway can have concurrent process writers.
Removing the locked append rescan or post-append projection reads without evidence that the replacement preserves current-head, idempotency, fencing, and projection behavior.
Treating the single-writer cache as wholly unimplemented; the current code already enables it in the per-lineage single-writer effect dispatcher.

Treating the packet's 834-second and 841-second lower bounds as interchangeable without checking run records.

Treating a profile description in prose as access to the profile's per-file measurements.
Claiming a wall-time reduction from step order alone without accounting for repeated setup/build and measuring the complete workflow.
